title: Maximize Score After N Operations
summary: Given an array nums of size 2 * n, perform n operations where in the i-th operation, choose two elements x and y, score i * gcd(x, y), and remove x and y.
statement: Given an array nums of size 2 * n, perform n operations where in the i-th operation, choose two elements x and y, score i * gcd(x, y), and remove x and y. Return the maximum possible score after n operations. The gcd(x, y) is the greatest common divisor of x and y.
constraints: The array has even length at most fourteen; each element is removed exactly once.
At one-indexed operation i, a chosen pair contributes i times its gcd; maximize total score.
hints: The future depends only on which indices have already been used.
Use a bitmask DP and add every possible unused pair as the next operation.
The operation number is half the used-bit count plus one.
Each pairing order corresponds to one path through masks, and maximizing every transition explores all legal schedules without recomputing equivalent used sets.
editorial: Each pairing order corresponds to one path through masks, and maximizing every transition explores all legal schedules without recomputing equivalent used sets.

tests.explanation: The only pair has gcd one and is chosen at operation one.
Pair 3 with 6 first and 4 with 8 second for score 3+8=11.
